newsitem.title: USA: US debt fund managers get more bullish-MCM survey.
newsitem.headline: US debt fund managers get more bullish-MCM survey.

text.p: U.S. fixed-income managers boosted durations to a new high over the past week, according to an MCM MoneyWatch Inc survey.
"Bullishness prevails, if one looks at positions, with durations" as a percentage of benchmark, said MCM money market analyst Peter McTeague, who conducts the asset allocation survey.
The weekly survey showed durations as a percentage of benchmark rose to 107.3 percent in the week ended November 4 from 106.7 percent in the prior week.
A duration reading above 100 percent indicates the group of investors polled is mostly long on the market.
"Survey durations are at a new high, with not an apparent worry in sight," added McTeague.
A portfolio's duration represents its average maturity and is used by portfolio managers to calculate exposure to risk.
In the "next likely move" category, portfolio managers representing 24 percent of total assets in the survey said they would "buy," up from 15 percent the prior week.
Strategists leaning toward "sell" fell to 24 percent, down from 28 percent in the week ended October 28.
Fifty-two percent of managers said they were "neutral" on the market, down from 57 percent a week ago.
Cash as a percentage of assets fell to 2.40 percent, against 2.60 percent registered the previous week.

The survey showed 19 percent of investors polled overweighted the 10-plus years duration sector, down from 20 percent the previous week, while 26 percent underweighted it. The remaining 55 percent were "neutral."
In the five- to 10-year duration sector, 57 percent of investors polled said they overweighted the securities and 14 percent underweighted them.
The survey included 40 domestic participants, who manage about $100 billion in fixed-income assets. The poll is conducted weekly by MCM and usually is released on Tuesday.
